newsitem.title: USA: Ocean Reef offers $60 million for Best Products.
newsitem.headline: Ocean Reef offers $60 million for Best Products.

text.p: Ocean Reef Management Inc., an investment firm, said Tuesday it launched a takeover bid valued at more than $60 million for the struggling catalogue retailer Best Products Co.
Under the proposal, Ocean Reef would offer $2 a share for Best Products' common stock, which is a premium of nearly 53 percent to the Richmond, Va.-based firm's stock price at last Friday's close.
Best Products has slightly more than 30 million shares outstanding, according to Ocean Reef.
Following the news, Best Products' stock gained 36 cents to $1.67 on the Nasdaq market.

"I think there is a real opportunity to transform this company from a catalogue retailer into a speciality retailer," said Rachmil Lekach, chairman of Ocean Reef, which recently completed the acquisition of retailer L. Luria & Son Inc.
Best Products has been struggling over the past several years. It emerged from bankruptcy in June 1994.
The company, which operates 169 stores in 23 states, lost $95.7 million in its fiscal year ended on Feb. 3. That was Best Products' second-largest loss in its history.
